items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Israel was showing how to hold my hand correct

ctx.x: says the reason he switched over to bass, how can he play like that -- and a whole lot of altos had put their horns down because of it. Not really, but they would say, well, what's the use? Everybody expects you to sound like Bird Berg, and if you did, you were copying.

Now there was a whole lot of musicians who hate to copy, you know, the creative musicians. I mean, that wasn't it. Just like, me, speaking about myself, now I loved Blanton, I loved him, and I took a little bit from Blanton, took a little bit from Israel Crosby and I put a little bit of Wilbur Ware in there, so I believe I got my own little way of playing, you know? So that's me. I don't find, like I hear people come up, saying, "You don't sound like so and so and so and so .." and I say, "Yeah, I have to sound…

I had a good friend of mine, a young bassist -- a Malachi Favors, with the Chicago Art Ensemble, and Maul brilliant young bassist, younger than I am Wilbur and he used to come for me every morning, and say, "Let's just play something for me." He stayed maybe 2 or 3 blocks from where I was living in Chicago during that time, '48, and I played and he was learning. You know, I'd show him what I knew, and now like I say, technically, I didn't know too much, but playing around -- Israel was showing how to hold my hand…
